CVX.rationale: Chevron is a high-quality integrated energy major with a wide moat, strong balance sheet, but the current setup is mixed. Fundamentals are solid — record production of 4.05M boepd in Q4 2025, strong operating cash flow of $10.8B, and a 25+ year dividend growth streak with ~3.8% yield. The integrated model provides natural hedging across commodity cycles. However, Q3 2025 showed YoY EPS decline of -26.6% and net income down -19.6%, reflecting the cyclical nature of the business. The Q1 2026 pre-announcement flagged $2.7-3.7B negative timing effects and a $350-400M legal charge, creating near-term earnings noise. Valuation is the key concern: P/E has expanded from ~15x in April 2025 to ~28x currently, near the top of its 365-day range (14.6-31.9x), while net margins have compressed from 8.5% to 6.6% and ROE from 10.7% to 6.6%. The stock is trading at a significant premium to its own recent history despite weaker profitability metrics. The Iran/Strait of Hormuz geopolitical situation has driven oil to ~$99/barrel, providing a tailwind, but much of this appears priced in given the valuation expansion. The upcoming May 1 earnings call is a potential catalyst, but Q1 results will be messy. California regulatory risks and potential refining exit add uncertainty. The stock's 12.6% quarterly gain and elevated P/E suggest the market has already priced in much of the upside from elevated oil prices. Mildly positive due to quality franchise and geopolitical tailwind, but capped by rich valuation vs history.
